title: Predicting Blood Concentration of Tacrolimus in Patients With Autoimmune Diseases Using Machine Learning Techniques Based on Real-World Evidence
summary: Among 193 tacrolimus therapeutic-drug-monitoring observations from 123 patients with autoimmune diseases, XGBoost was the best-performing one of 14 tested models for predicting blood concentration (R²=0.54). This retrospective cohort result does not establish improved dosing or clinical outcomes.
ai_technology: Supervised machine-learning models use patient and treatment variables to predict tacrolimus blood concentration.
organization: University of Tsukuba; Tsukuba Medical Center Hospital

source_review.scope: Primary source full text, including Methods and Results; first result-bearing version checked against primary publication metadata.

evidence.tested: Models were trained and assessed using observations from 123 patients; XGBoost reported R² 0.54.
evidence.unknown: Small retrospective dataset without external validation; dosing utility and patient outcomes were not tested.
